title: Marketplace Listing Refresh — Launch Brief (Draft)
body:
Doc status: DRAFT (for internal review)
Owner: Camila Reyes (Marketing) / Soojin Lee (PMM)
Primary goal: Publish refreshed AWS + GCP Marketplace listings + SKUs, with a procurement-friendly story that preserves a developer-first activation experience.

1) Executive summary
We are refreshing Redwood Inference’s AWS Marketplace and GCP Cloud Marketplace presence to:
- Make enterprise procurement easier (committed spend, PO/invoicing, standard vendor workflows)
- Launch new SKU taxonomy aligned to Redwood Hosted API, Dedicated, Private, plus add-ons (compliance/retention/premium SLA where applicable)
- Reduce buyer friction post-purchase by improving purchase → entitlement → org linking → first request
- Increase marketplace-sourced pipeline and improve conversion from marketplace interest to activated Redwood orgs

This brief covers: (a) announcement plan, (b) internal enablement plan and dates, (c) customer comms, and (d) metrics + instrumentation from marketplace lead → activation.

2) Launch scope (what is included)
In-scope deliverables
- AWS Marketplace listing refresh: updated copy, keywords, screenshots, pricing/SKU table, attachments (security packet references)
- GCP Marketplace listing refresh: updated solution description, deployment/provisioning instructions, FAQs (GCP formatting requirements)
- Marketplace SKU set: Hosted API / Dedicated / Private + add-ons; consistent naming across AWS/GCP + Redwood Console + internal billing descriptors
- Docs updates for buyers:
  - AWS Marketplace onboarding page + FAQ
  - GCP Marketplace onboarding page + FAQ
  - Procurement-oriented FAQ on pricing/packaging pages (link-outs)
- Internal enablement:
  - Sales/SE talk track + SKU selection guidance
  - Support/CS troubleshooting guide and macros
  - “What to collect from buyer” checklist (account IDs, org ID, region, entitlement status)
- Measurement:
  - Attribution and lifecycle tracking (marketplace source → lead → purchase → entitlement → activation)
  - Dashboard for entitlement lag + provisioning errors (SRE/Support)

Out of scope (explicit)
- Major billing re-platform (only minimal changes to support new marketplace SKUs)
- Broad product feature work unrelated to marketplace onboarding

3) Target audiences and positioning
Primary buyer personas (marketplace motion)
- Procurement-led enterprise buyers who want committed spend through cloud marketplaces
- Security/compliance stakeholders evaluating vendor posture (SOC2/ISO stance, encryption, audit logs, residency statements)
- Technical evaluators who want fast activation and clear setup steps

Positioning (high-level)
- Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform optimized for production economics: latency, reliability, and cost controls across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Marketplace listings emphasize: predictable procurement + predictable serving.

Messaging guardrails
- Security claims must match the Security FAQ + approved packet language.
- Avoid absolute statements (“fully compliant with every standard”); use precise wording (“SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA”, “encryption in transit and at rest”, etc.)
- Residency/retention wording must align to actual product controls and documented regions.

4) Launch approach (soft launch → public launch)
We are planning a two-phase launch to control risk:
Phase 1: Soft launch (silent publish + limited field enablement)
- Listings go live (or updated versions approved) with no broad external announcement
- Enable internal teams (Sales/SE/CS/Support) and monitor provisioning + entitlement lag
- Validate attribution and funnel metrics end-to-end

Phase 2: Public launch (announcement + outbound)
- Publish a short announcement to drive qualified marketplace traffic
- Update website CTAs and docs navigation
- Route inbound leads with clear “buy via marketplace” path

Proposed go/no-go criteria
- Marketplace review approval received from AWS and GCP partner teams
- Security packet approved by Dr. Aisha Rahman / Olga Petrov per internal workflow
- Docs pages published and validated (ENG-4404 / ENG-4405)
- Monitoring dashboards live (webhook failures, entitlement lag timers, provisioning error rate) (ENG-4407)
- Support runbooks + escalation paths validated (ENG-4409)
- Sales enablement assets in place (internal deck + talk track)

5) Timeline (draft) + owners
NOTE: exact external dates depend on AWS/GCP review lead times; below is the internal target cadence.

Week 0 (now) — Finalize content + tracking plan
- Listing copy finalization: Soojin Lee (PMM) + Camila Reyes
- Security packet final language: Marcus Lin + Olga Petrov + Dr. Aisha Rahman
- SKU naming and mapping validation: Nikhil Sharma / Lauren Bishop / Vivek Kulkarni + Cole Summers
- Instrumentation spec: Ben Carter + Nadia Rahman + Ethan Park

Week 1 — Submission + internal enablement prep
- Submit AWS listing updates + attachments: Partnerships owner (via vendor portal); tracked in partner feedback log
- Submit GCP listing updates: Partnerships owner
- Finalize internal enablement slides: Markus Klein (SE) + Jordan Blake org input
- Support macros and troubleshooting guide updates: Dev Patel + Jasmine Liu

Week 2 — Soft launch (silent publish) + monitoring
- Publish docs updates + validate redirects/nav: Elliot Price + Kira Thompson
- Release onboarding flow updates behind flag/canary: Connor O’Brien + Talia Benson + Engineering leads
- Turn on dashboards/alerts: Rafael Mendes + Allison Grant

Week 3 — Public launch (if metrics look healthy)
- External announcement (lightweight): Camila Reyes + Soojin Lee
- Update website CTA (where applicable): Marketing Ops (Ben Carter support for tracking)
- Sales-wide enablement session: Markus Klein + Soojin Lee

6) Announcement plan (external)
Goal
Drive qualified buyers who prefer cloud marketplace procurement to the updated listings and a clear activation path.

Primary channel options (pick based on readiness)
- Redwood blog post (short): “Buy Redwood Inference via AWS Marketplace and Google Cloud Marketplace”
- Docs banner / “Procurement” section updates
- LinkedIn post(s) from company page + exec reposts (Camila/Evelyn/Jordan as appropriate)
- Email to existing procurement-stage opportunities who requested marketplace path (Sales-led, not broad blast)

What we are NOT doing (at least initially)
- Broad product launch press push (this is a packaging + procurement/activation improvement)
- Aggressive paid spend until we confirm conversion + support load

Draft external copy points (placeholders; align with messaging framework)
- “Procurement-friendly buying through AWS/GCP marketplaces”
- “Clear SKU catalog for Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments”
- “Faster activation: purchase → entitlement → org linking → first request”
- “Security documentation and audit-ready controls available for review”

Required links
- AWS Marketplace listing URL (final)
- GCP Marketplace listing URL (final)
- Docs: AWS Marketplace onboarding
- Docs: GCP Marketplace onboarding
- Contact: marketplace procurement help alias (route to Sales/CS)

7) Internal enablement plan
Audience: Sales, Solutions Engineering, Customer Success, Support, Partnerships, Finance/Legal

Enablement assets
- “Buying Redwood via Cloud Marketplaces” internal deck (outline exists): owner Markus Klein
- SKU selection one-pager: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private + when to route direct contract: owner Soojin Lee (+ Finance/Legal review)
- Security FAQ (AWS/GCP): owner Naomi Feldman + Security reviewers
- Support troubleshooting playbook + macros: owner Dev Patel

Enablement session agenda (60 min)
- Marketplace procurement flow (AWS + GCP) and what info to collect
- SKU taxonomy and add-ons (what’s included vs line item)
- Demo: purchase → org linking (Console) → first API call
- Common failure modes and escalation path
- Discounting constraints / when direct contract is recommended (Finance/Legal guidance)

Internal comms
- #sales: talk track + FAQ link + escalation notes
- #support: top ticket categories + macros
- #eng-sre: dashboards + oncall notes during soft launch

8) Customer comms plan (direct, targeted)
Who we will proactively contact
- Existing customers asking to move spend to marketplace (expansion/procurement-driven)
- Late-stage prospects with procurement blockers where marketplace solves PO/invoicing

Comms format
- 1:1 email from AE/SE with:
  - Marketplace listing link(s)
  - “How to activate” docs link
  - What information we need to map entitlements to a Redwood org (e.g., cloud account IDs)
  - SLA/support expectations and how to request security packet under NDA

Customer-facing FAQ topics to include (public docs)
- How marketplace purchase maps to Redwood orgs and entitlements
- Expected time to entitlement activation; what to do if delayed
- Upgrades/downgrades and plan changes (policy TBD; must align with PM-876)
- Regions/residency constraints and what happens if there’s a region mismatch
- Support contacts and required information for faster triage

9) Metrics + instrumentation plan (marketplace lead → activation)
Owners
- Ben Carter (Growth): attribution + HubSpot routing
- Nadia Rahman (Metering/Cost attribution): internal event taxonomy
- Ethan Park (Entitlements): marketplace event ingestion correctness
- Rafael Mendes / Allison Grant (SRE/Observability): dashboards/alerts

Funnel definition (working)
A) Awareness/Interest
- Marketplace listing impressions (where available)
- Listing page views
- Click-through to Redwood docs or console

B) Lead / Intent capture
- “Contact sales” / “Request private offer” form submissions sourced from marketplace pages
- Inbound leads tagged as marketplace (HubSpot source)

C) Purchase
- Marketplace subscription/purchase event (AWS/GCP)

D) Provisioning
- Entitlement received by Redwood webhook ingestion
- Entitlement mapped to internal plan code + add-ons
- Org linking completed in Console

E) Activation
- First successful API call (or first token streamed) after entitlement
- Time-to-first-request (TTFR) from purchase
- Activation rate within 24h / 7d

Core success metrics (initial targets are directional; to be finalized)
- Purchase → entitlement received: p50 < 5 min, p95 < 30 min
- Entitlement received → org linked: p50 < 10 min (assuming user attempts)
- Purchase → first successful request: p50 < 30 min (for Hosted API SKU)
- Support ticket rate: < 3% of purchases generating a support ticket in first 7 days
- Marketplace-sourced pipeline: baseline + uplift post-launch (tracked monthly)

Instrumentation requirements
Attribution (web/marketing)
- Ensure marketplace-related links use consistent UTMs:
  - utm_source=aws_marketplace | gcp_marketplace
  - utm_medium=marketplace
  - utm_campaign=marketplace_refresh_2025
- Confirm routing into HubSpot with lifecycle stage and “Marketplace interest” property
- Create a dashboard that shows marketplace leads → opps → closed won (time lag acknowledged)

Product/Console events
- Console events:
  - marketplace_onboarding_viewed
  - marketplace_org_link_started
  - marketplace_org_link_success
  - marketplace_org_link_error (include reason code)
- Entitlement pipeline events:
  - marketplace_webhook_received (provider=aws|gcp)
  - marketplace_webhook_validation_failed
  - entitlement_created
  - entitlement_mapped_to_plan
  - entitlement_activation_completed
- API activation events:
  - first_successful_request_after_entitlement (record time delta)

Operational metrics (SRE)
- Webhook failure rate by provider
- Entitlement lag timer (purchase/subscription timestamp to activation)
- Provisioning error rate, by reason:
  - region mismatch
  - duplicate subscription
  - org not found
  - entitlement not recognized (SKU mapping)
  - validation failure

Reporting cadence
- Daily during soft launch (first 5 business days)
- Weekly for the first month post-public launch

10) Support readiness + escalation
Primary anticipated ticket categories
- Entitlement activation delay
- Wrong org linked / multiple org confusion
- Region mismatch (GCP particularly)
- Billing/invoice confusion marketplace vs direct contract

Escalation path (draft)
- L1 Support: Dev Patel team
- L2 Provisioning/Entitlements: Ethan Park / Cole Summers on rotation
- SRE escalation: Rafael Mendes for sustained webhook failures or lag spikes
- Security questions: Marcus Lin / Olga Petrov (evidence sharing under NDA)

Required internal runbooks
- “How to verify entitlement status” (by provider)
- “How to reprocess webhook / backfill entitlement” (idempotent)
- “How to move entitlement to correct org” (with audit log requirements)

11) Risks and mitigations
Risk: Marketplace review delays or changing requirements
- Mitigation: maintain partner feedback log; keep screenshots + security packet ready; respond within 24h

Risk: SKU naming inconsistencies across AWS/GCP and Redwood Console/billing
- Mitigation: lock naming via ADR + mapping sheet; block launch until UI strings match

Risk: Over-promising security/compliance posture in listing copy
- Mitigation: security claim review gate by Dr. Aisha Rahman / Marcus Lin; use approved FAQ language

Risk: Entitlement lag causes buyer frustration and support load
- Mitigation: dashboards + alerts, clear docs and in-console messaging, retries/idempotency, defined escalation

12) Open questions (to resolve before public launch)
- Final upgrade/downgrade policy for marketplace buyers (PM-876): what can be self-serve vs requires support
- Are we launching all add-ons as separate marketplace line items on both AWS and GCP, or bundling differs by provider?
- Final public support contact and SLA language for marketplace buyers (what is included vs premium SLA add-on)
- Final decision on announcement scope: docs-only vs blog + LinkedIn

Appendix A — Draft internal go/no-go checklist (short)
- Copy approved (PMM + Legal where needed)
- Security packet approved + evidence-sharing process documented
- Docs published + tested
- Console onboarding flow stable in production
- Dashboards/alerts on and verified
- Support macros ready
- Sales enablement session completed

Appendix B — Notes to self (working)
- Once listing URLs are final, replace placeholders in docs + deck + internal macros.
- Ensure the “Request Private Offer” path is consistent across AWS/GCP and routes to the right sales queue.
- Confirm with Finance (Laura Bennett/Rishi Malhotra) the language for credits/discount constraints in marketplace terms.
